Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name reservation; Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) at the registered office for registration and inscription.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) – arts. 20-23 (public deed constitution), art. 28 (registered office), arts. 36-69 (minimum capital and contributions), arts. 124-125 (corporate purpose). Also Royal Decree 1483/2012 (General Accounting Plan).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de Constitución (notarised deed of incorporation) registered in the Mercantile Registry; accompanied by Form 036 for the provisional Tax Identification Code (NIF).

Incorporation processing time

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

For an SL, the statutory minimum is €3,000, fully subscribed and paid at execution of the public deed. The amount must be deposited in a bank account opened in the future company's name and evidenced by a bank certificate to the notary; no separate escrow account or escrow agent is required. The deposit becomes freely available after registration.

Funding & unlock path:

Paid-in capital rule: For an SL, the statutory minimum is €3,000, fully subscribed and paid at execution of the public deed. The amount must be deposited in a bank account opened in the future company's name and evidenced by a bank certificate to the notary; no separate escrow account or escrow agent is required. The deposit becomes freely available after registration.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the AEAT Electronic Office (Sede Electrónica). The common Spanish VAT and corporate tax regime applies in mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands; the Basque Country and Navarra have separate historical tax administrations, and the Canary Islands apply IGIC rather than mainland Spanish VAT.

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF and then a definitive NIF through the AEAT, normally using Form 036, with incorporation deed, articles of association, Commercial Registry evidence, registered address, and identification of directors and authorized representatives. A foreign entity carrying on taxable activities or required to interact with Spanish tax authorities must obtain a Spanish NIF, generally by filing Form 036 with the competent AEAT office or through an authorized representative. Foreign corporate documents must normally be legalized or apostilled, accompanied by an official Spanish translation where required, and include evidence of the entity's legal existence, registered address, ownership or control information where requested, and the powers and tax identification of its representative. A Spanish VAT number is the Spanish NIF prefixed by ES and is activated through registration in the Census of Business Persons, Professionals and Withholding Agents. Registration should be completed before commencing taxable activities, making intra-Community acquisitions or supplies, importing goods, or issuing invoices requiring Spanish VAT identification. The intra-Community VAT operator register (ROI/VIES) must be requested where intra-Community transactions require it. A non-established business may additionally need a Spanish fiscal representative for particular non-EU VAT refund or compliance procedures, although Spain generally does not impose a universal VAT fiscal-representative requirement on every non-established taxable person.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Spanish SL is a separate taxpayer for Spanish Corporate Income Tax and is generally taxed on its worldwide accounting profit, subject to statutory adjustments, exemptions, participation exemptions, loss utilization limits, transfer-pricing rules, and applicable tax treaties. Spanish tax residence generally follows incorporation under Spanish law, registered office, or effective management in Spain. The SL is not automatically fiscally transparent merely because it has limited liability. A Spanish SL may qualify for specific reduced rates or incentives, including regimes applicable to newly created entities, but those regimes do not convert it into a pass-through entity. — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF and then a definitive NIF through the AEAT, normally using Form 036, with incorporation deed, articles of association, Commercial Registry evidence, registered address, and identification of directors and authorized representatives. A foreign entity carrying on taxable activities or required to interact with Spanish tax authorities must obtain a Spanish NIF, generally by filing Form 036 with the competent AEAT office or through an authorized representative. Foreign corporate documents must normally be legalized or apostilled, accompanied by an official Spanish translation where required, and include evidence of the entity's legal existence, registered address, ownership or control information where requested, and the powers and tax identification of its representative. A Spanish VAT number is the Spanish NIF prefixed by ES and is activated through registration in the Census of Business Persons, Professionals and Withholding Agents. Registration should be completed before commencing taxable activities, making intra-Community acquisitions or supplies, importing goods, or issuing invoices requiring Spanish VAT identification. The intra-Community VAT operator register (ROI/VIES) must be requested where intra-Community transactions require it. A non-established business may additionally need a Spanish fiscal representative for particular non-EU VAT refund or compliance procedures, although Spain generally does not impose a universal VAT fiscal-representative requirement on every non-established taxable person.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation. A Spanish SL is a separate taxpayer for Spanish Corporate Income Tax and is generally taxed on its worldwide accounting profit, subject to statutory adjustments, exemptions, participation exemptions, loss utilization limits, transfer-pricing rules, and applicable tax treaties. Spanish tax residence generally follows incorporation under Spanish law, registered office, or effective management in Spain. The SL is not automatically fiscally transparent merely because it has limited liability. A Spanish SL may qualify for specific reduced rates or incentives, including regimes applicable to newly created entities, but those regimes do not convert it into a pass-through entity.

Available election forms

Spain has no United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. Separate legal entities are ordinarily subject to Corporate Income Tax. Available elections or optional regimes may include the Spanish consolidated Corporate Income Tax regime for qualifying groups, the special VAT group regime, the special VAT cash-accounting regime where statutory conditions are met, the monthly VAT refund regime and REDEME registration, and voluntary or mandatory SII reporting depending on taxpayer status. Certain transparent-entity, permanent-establishment, investment, restructuring, holding-company, and tax-haven rules may apply by operation of law or under specific statutory conditions. Spanish anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing ATAD 2 can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or restrict relief for payments involving hybrid entities, hybrid instruments, imported mismatches, or dual-resident arrangements; there is no general elective hybrid-mismatch classification.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0. Spain has no general turnover threshold below which a person making taxable economic activities is automatically outside VAT registration. A taxable person must register in the census before commencing a taxable activity or conducting transactions requiring VAT identification. Separate thresholds and conditions may apply to specific special schemes, distance sales, intra-Community acquisitions, imports, and EU-wide small-business rules. A hospital engineering EPC contractor must assess VAT registration, domestic reverse charge, intra-Community transactions, import VAT, and the place-of-supply rules for installation and construction-related services. The Spanish domestic reverse charge may apply to qualifying construction, installation, and subcontracting services connected with construction or rehabilitation works when statutory conditions are satisfied.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory export conditions are satisfied and the supplier retains reliable evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. The exemption is not available merely because the customer is non-resident or pays from a foreign bank account. Evidence normally includes the export customs declaration, MRN and electronic exit confirmation, transport documentation, commercial invoice, order and delivery records, and accounting records. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for the applicable VAT exemption where the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier satisfies recapitulative-statement and evidentiary requirements. Services supplied to a business established outside the EU are generally outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the business-to-business place-of-supply rule, rather than technically zero-rated; exceptions apply to services connected with immovable property, admission to events, passenger transport, short-term transport hiring, and other special categories. Export-related logistics, installation, and engineering services require transaction-specific place-of-supply analysis.

  • Electronic export customs declaration submitted through the Spanish customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
  • Electronic confirmation that the goods exited the EU customs territory, or equivalent customs-certified exit evidence
  • Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, Incoterms where used, and VAT treatment
  • Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or other transport document demonstrating dispatch to the non-EU destination
  • Purchase order, contract, packing list, delivery records, and warehouse or carrier evidence linking the goods to the export declaration
  • Accounting records, VAT books, export-sales ledger, and evidence of reporting in the relevant VAT return
  • Customer identification and, for intra-Community supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number and recapitulative-statement evidence
  • Bank payment or settlement evidence where relevant; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory Spanish VAT export document and does not substitute for customs exit evidence

Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every private-sector invoice. The electronic invoicing framework under Law 18/2022 and its implementing regulations will introduce mandatory B2B electronic invoicing in phases after the applicable technical and regulatory commencement dates. Public-sector supplies generally require structured electronic invoices through the designated public-sector platforms, including FACe where applicable. The SII system requires qualifying taxpayers, including large businesses, VAT groups, REDEME entities, and voluntary participants, to transmit VAT invoice-record data electronically to the AEAT, generally within four business days subject to statutory exclusions and adjustments. Tax software is subject to integrity, traceability, accessibility, and anti-tampering requirements under the invoicing-system rules, including Royal Decree 1007/2023 and subsequent implementation measures; applicable deadlines and technical requirements must be verified at deployment. Electronic signatures, QR or verification data, digital records, and retention controls may be required depending on the invoicing system and recipient. Electronic invoicing does not itself replace customs evidence, VAT books, or transaction-level proof of export.

Spain has no general 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement for claiming export VAT exemption or input-VAT recovery. Export proceeds may remain abroad subject to ordinary accounting, anti-money-laundering, customs, transfer-pricing, and financial-reporting obligations. AEAT audits focus on actual exit from the EU, consistency between customs and VAT records, transport evidence, customer status, correct place-of-supply treatment, and absence of sham or diverted transactions. If zero-rating or exemption is unsupported, the supplier may be required to pay the undercharged VAT retrospectively, together with late-payment interest and applicable surcharges, while input-VAT deductions or refunds may be denied or clawed back. Inaccurate or fraudulent VAT treatment can attract proportional tax penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly omitted or unduly refunded tax, depending on the infringement and aggravating circumstances, in addition to record-keeping and invoicing penalties. Deliberate tax fraud exceeding the criminal threshold of EUR 120,000 of tax per fiscal year may constitute a criminal offense under Spanish law, with potential fines and imprisonment. Customs penalties, seizure, loss of preferential treatment, and coordinated VAT recovery may also apply where export documentation is falsified or goods did not leave the EU.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain maintains full current-account and capital-account liberalisation under Article 63 TFEU and Title IV of Royal Decree 1816/1991; the euro is fully convertible and no prior exchange-control authorisation applies to equity injections, profit remittances, supplier payments or shareholder loans. Dividends and branch profits are remittable after the 25% corporate income tax levy, subject to Non-Resident Income Tax withholding at the statutory 19% for EU/EEA and treaty-eligible recipients, or a reduced DTT rate under Spain's Latin American treaties (typically 5%-15% for substantial shareholdings); 21% applies only to non-cooperative tax-haven jurisdictions. A post-investment foreign-investment declaration to the DGCTI is required when the inbound investment exceeds EUR 1,250,000 or reaches 10% of the SL capital; this filing is statistical and not an authorisation bar. No capital controls, quarantine periods, or prior clearance delays apply to euro-denominated or foreign-currency movements through resident banks.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no statutory surrender obligation, a 0% mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export proceeds; exporters may retain 100% of receipts in EUR or foreign-currency settlement accounts held domestically or abroad. The only binding rule is statistical: foreign-trade settlements exceeding EUR 1,250,000 per settlement event must be declared to Banco de España under Order ETD/22/2023 (replacing the former EUR 50,000 per-operation threshold), and all settlements remain subject to standard invoicing, customs-export documentation and transfer-pricing substance rules. A 90-day conversion into EUR is recommended treasury policy, not law, to neutralise EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm-currency volatility on the EPC working-capital cycle.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), the national central bank within the Eurosystem, exercises monetary operations, balance-of-payments statistics and the foreign-transaction declaration regime under Royal Decree 1835/2010. Foreign-investment screening and registry functions are attributed to the Directorate General for International Trade and Investments (DGCTI) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business; the exchange-control legal framework is completed by Article 63 TFEU, Royal Decree 1816/1991, and Order ETD/22/2023.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for EUR pass-through disbursement rails; LOW for statutory banking instruments. A foreign-authorised digital EMI (e.g., UK, Lithuania, Germany) cannot settle Healthcare_Authority_Wire payments because Spanish public-health treasuries disburse through Iberpay/TARGET2, an infrastructure to which non-member EMIs lack direct access. EMIs are also legally incapable of issuing 'avales' or 'garantías definitivas' required under Spanish public procurement (Law 9/2017 on Public Sector Contracts) and cannot hold irrevocable escrow/retention mandates for hospital EPC works. A Banco de España-registered or EU-passported EMI may open an ES IBAN for operational overheads, but the SL must maintain its primary treasury relationship, contract guarantees and hedging lines with a fully licensed Spanish credit institution.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) resident outside the EU, or a corporate chain containing a nominee/offshore layer, triggering a higher-risk classification under Article 4 of Law 10/2010 and EBA risk-factor guidelines.

Root cause: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) resident outside the EU, or a corporate chain containing a nominee/offshore layer, triggering a higher-risk classification under Article 4 of Law 10/2010 and EBA risk-factor guidelines.

Defense evidence: Apostilled parent certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing; full corporate-organisation chart to final natural persons; tax residence certificates of all UBOs; notarised source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; three years of audited ultimate-parent financial statements or a certified book-debt declaration; written narrative on the EPC hospital-medical-gas pipeline business, public-health payer base, and ISIC/NAICS scope.
Equity capital wired before the capital increase is inscribed in the Registro Mercantil, a pattern flagged as potential front-loading of unverified funds.

Root cause: Equity capital wired before the capital increase is inscribed in the Registro Mercantil, a pattern flagged as potential front-loading of unverified funds.

Defense evidence: Public deed of capital increase (escritura de ampliación de capital); the notary's certificate of cash deposit (certificación del desembolso) required by Article 62 of the Capital Companies Law; a dated board commitment to file for inscription within the statutory 2-month window; a copy of the Banco de España foreign-transaction declaration and, where applicable, the DGCTI foreign-investment filing reference.
High-velocity pay-outs to non-EU equipment suppliers (copper tube, vacuum pumps, terminal manifolds) without an evidentiary chain, creating a trade-mismatch red flag.

Root cause: High-velocity pay-outs to non-EU equipment suppliers (copper tube, vacuum pumps, terminal manifolds) without an evidentiary chain, creating a trade-mismatch red flag.

Defense evidence: Bundle of purchase orders, supplier commercial invoices, CMR/Bill of Lading, DUA/SAD customs declarations and inspection certificates; ISO 7396-1 and UNE 7396-1 medical-gas-system compliance certificates; bank-purpose narrative 'pago de importación de bienes de equipo sanitario'; matching letter-of-credit or documentary-collection records.
Receipts routed through intermediaries from Latin American hospital or health-ministry payers, triggering PEP and sanctions-led enhanced due diligence.

Root cause: Receipts routed through intermediaries from Latin American hospital or health-ministry payers, triggering PEP and sanctions-led enhanced due diligence.

Defense evidence: Certified copy of the public-procurement award or framework contract with the health authority; PEP questionnaire and identity evidence of the payer's authorised signatory; certification of works (certificación de obra) and payment certificates; where relevant, the EIB/IDB/CAF or development-bank funding agreement evidencing the disbursement chain; a sanctions legal opinion (EU, UK, OFAC) covering the counterparty jurisdiction and project corridor.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant routing: (1) segregate shareholder funds in the originator's account; (2) send an SWIFT MT103 wire to the SL's Spanish IBAN with the memo 'Aportación de capital — escritura de ampliación de capital de [date]', settling in EUR via SEPA/EBA or TARGET2; (3) file the applicable Banco de España foreign-transaction declaration (declaración de operaciones con el exterior) for the inflow and, when the investment exceeds EUR 1,250,000 or 10% ownership, file the DGCTI post-investment declaration through the electronic registry within the statutory window; (4) retain the notarial certificate of deposit as the bank's compliance evidence pack. For shareholder loans, execute a documented 'préstamo participativo' or ordinary shareholder-loan agreement, disclose the lender's Spanish NIF, and clear interest and principal remittances against the same declaration framework; treaty-favourable withholding requires the lender's tax residence certificate and a beneficial-ownership statement.Primary clearing rails: (a) SEPA Credit Transfer through Iberpay for Spanish and EU suppliers — the same rail used by hospital treasuries for Healthcare_Authority_Wire settlement of the SL's progress certificates; (b) SWIFT MT103 for extra-SEPA suppliers and payments above EUR 50,000; (c) Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 (issued via SWIFT MT700) for high-value imports of manifolds, vacuum pumps and copper systems, with confirmation requested where the supplier's bank requires it; (d) Documentary Collections (CAD) for routine Latin American vendor shipments. Contract retentions must be parked in an escrow/guarantee account pledged to the hospital authority by an irrevocable 'mandato de disposición de garantía'; treasury must reconcile certification-triggered settlements monthly to avoid VAT and corporate-income-tax timing mismatches.FX Forwards ('seguros de cambio') with Spanish or EU-licensed banks, tenors up to 12 months, documented against underlying EPC contracts and invoices, executed under ISDA or FBF master agreements and subject to EMIR trade reporting.Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on non-fully-convertible Latin American currencies (COP, MXN, PEN) where physical offshore settlement is impossible, supported by underlying tender and contract exposure dossiers.Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) converting project-finance liabilities from EUR into USD or LatAm-currency baskets, subject to EMIR reporting and clearing-threshold assessment.European-style currency options to cap tender and bid-stage exposure on hospital-authority projects, with premiums capitalised into bid pricing.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for EUR pass-through disbursement rails; LOW for statutory banking instruments. A foreign-authorised digital EMI (e.g., UK, Lithuania, Germany) cannot settle Healthcare_Authority_Wire payments because Spanish public-health treasuries disburse through Iberpay/TARGET2, an infrastructure to which non-member EMIs lack direct access. EMIs are also legally incapable of issuing 'avales' or 'garantías definitivas' required under Spanish public procurement (Law 9/2017 on Public Sector Contracts) and cannot hold irrevocable escrow/retention mandates for hospital EPC works. A Banco de España-registered or EU-passported EMI may open an ES IBAN for operational overheads, but the SL must maintain its primary treasury relationship, contract guarantees and hedging lines with a fully licensed Spanish credit institution.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end; for a December year-end entity, filing window runs from 1 July to 25 July. Quarterly interim prepayments (Modelo 202 or 222) filed during the taxable year based on prior-year taxable income, with payment in April, July, October, and December.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 108 Net turnover reported in the financial year A non-resident Spanish SL must report gross turnover generated through its Spanish permanent establishment or Spanish-source activities, in euros, with no netting of expenses. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: penalty of 10% of the untendered amount if filed within 3 months after the deadline, plus 1% for each additional month of delay. After an AEAT formal request: 50% penalty of the payment due, with reduced surcharges if filed within 3 months of notification, escalating to 100% surcharge after 12 months. Late filing also accrues late payment interest (interés de demora) of 4.0625% for 2025, and a minimum fixed penalty may apply. For entities with a tax amount exceeding €15,000, failure to file by electronic means carries a separate formal infringement penalty of €400 to €2,000.
Box 200 Corporate income tax base (base imponible), prior to offset of tax losses Non-resident entity computes Spanish PE attributable profits under the separate enterprise principle; all intercompany transactions must reflect arm's length consideration. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: penalty of 10% of the untendered amount if filed within 3 months after the deadline, plus 1% for each additional month of delay. After an AEAT formal request: 50% penalty of the payment due, with reduced surcharges if filed within 3 months of notification, escalating to 100% surcharge after 12 months. Late filing also accrues late payment interest (interés de demora) of 4.0625% for 2025, and a minimum fixed penalty may apply. For entities with a tax amount exceeding €15,000, failure to file by electronic means carries a separate formal infringement penalty of €400 to €2,000.
Box 302 Tax loss carryforwards generated in prior years offset in the current period Non-resident SL may offset tax losses attributable to the Spanish PE, limited to 50% of the tax base for entities with net revenue over €20 million; entities under that threshold may offset up to 60% in 2025 and must wait until after the 5-year carryforward period. Offsetting cannot reduce the tax base below 50% of the pre-offset amount for entities meeting the revenue threshold, or below 25% for other entities. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: penalty of 10% of the untendered amount if filed within 3 months after the deadline, plus 1% for each additional month of delay. After an AEAT formal request: 50% penalty of the payment due, with reduced surcharges if filed within 3 months of notification, escalating to 100% surcharge after 12 months. Late filing also accrues late payment interest (interés de demora) of 4.0625% for 2025, and a minimum fixed penalty may apply. For entities with a tax amount exceeding €15,000, failure to file by electronic means carries a separate formal infringement penalty of €400 to €2,000.
Box 435 Foreign tax credits and double taxation relief applied Non-resident company can claim credit for withholding taxes suffered in Spain on income attributable to the PE and may apply DTA relief on dividends, interest, and royalties subject to a valid certificate of tax residence in the treaty state. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: penalty of 10% of the untendered amount if filed within 3 months after the deadline, plus 1% for each additional month of delay. After an AEAT formal request: 50% penalty of the payment due, with reduced surcharges if filed within 3 months of notification, escalating to 100% surcharge after 12 months. Late filing also accrues late payment interest (interés de demora) of 4.0625% for 2025, and a minimum fixed penalty may apply. For entities with a tax amount exceeding €15,000, failure to file by electronic means carries a separate formal infringement penalty of €400 to €2,000.
Box 559 Total amount payable or resulting refund Where a non-resident SL has no PE, income subject to non-resident income tax (IRNR) must be reported on Modelo 210; where a PE exists, the annual Modelo 200 is final settlement and quarterly Modelo 202 prepayments apply to the PE's taxable income. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: penalty of 10% of the untendered amount if filed within 3 months after the deadline, plus 1% for each additional month of delay. After an AEAT formal request: 50% penalty of the payment due, with reduced surcharges if filed within 3 months of notification, escalating to 100% surcharge after 12 months. Late filing also accrues late payment interest (interés de demora) of 4.0625% for 2025, and a minimum fixed penalty may apply. For entities with a tax amount exceeding €15,000, failure to file by electronic means carries a separate formal infringement penalty of €400 to €2,000.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 1,000,000

Economic substance scope: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to the extent that Spanish transfer pricing law under Article 18 of Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades mandates that related-party transactions be valued at arm's length. Spain does not operate Caribbean-style ESR but the general anti-abuse rule (cláusula antielusión), substance-over-form doctrine under Article 13 of the General Tax Law, and the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) require the Spanish SL to maintain real business activity, physical presence proportionate to the hospital engineering EPC activity, qualified personnel, contractual substance, and economic ownership of assets and risks. A Spanish SL without adequate substance that merely channels medical gas pipeline installation back-to-back contracts is vulnerable to recharacterization under anti-abuse rules and denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT).

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion (Infracción Tributaria Grave / Delito contra la Hacienda Pública)

Statutory sanction: Criminal tax offence (art. 305 Código Penal) punishable by imprisonment from 2 to 6 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount. Additionally, loss of entitlement to public subsidies, tax benefits, and government contracts for a period of up to 6 years. For non-criminal serious infringement, a proportional penalty between 50% and 100% of the tax amount plus late payment interest.

Director personal liability: Directors can be personally liable under the doctrine of levantamiento del velo (piercing of the corporate veil) for civil restitution to the tax authority, jointly and severally with the SL. Criminal liability extends personally to de facto and de jure administrators who knowingly ordered or facilitated the evasion; the court may impose travel bans within Spain and the Schengen area, seizure of personal assets, restriction on freedom of movement, and imprisonment. Tax liability can be shifted to personal assets under art. 42 Ley General Tributaria where the director caused or collaborated in the infringement.
Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Entidad Carente de Sustancia)

Statutory sanction: Recharacterization of imputed income; denial of tax residence benefits; denial of treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary / Interest-Royalty Directive relief; application of anti-abuse clause (art. 15 LIS) to disregard the legal form; potential imposition of tax on deemed income, plus late payment interest and penalties of 50% to 100% of the associated tax deficiency. Spanish General Tax Law art. 206 bis contains a specific sanction for abusive arrangements of up to 25% on the transaction amount.

Director personal liability: Directors who signed certificates of substance falsifying economic presence are personally liable for the tax debt and may be charged with falsification of company records under art. 390 Código Penal, subject to imprisonment from 3 to 6 years and disqualification from holding directorship positions in Spain. Travel restrictions and extradition proceedings may be ordered by the competent criminal court.
Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Deficiency

Statutory sanction: Correction of the tax base to arm's length value, application of an additional penalty of 15% of the corrected amount where documentation is absent or inaccurate, plus late payment interest. In cases where the corrected transaction is considered a sham, the adjustment may attract a 50% penalty. Transfer pricing documentation may trigger a formal requirement to submit Modelo 232 (annual related-party transaction return) with a filing deadline of 10 months after the fiscal year-end; each omission or inaccurate transaction carries a minimum penalty of €1,000, escalating up to €100,000 for hidden related-party transactions.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly signed false transfer pricing studies or deliberately arranged overpricing may be jointly liable for the penalty under art. 42 LGT. In a criminal tax qualification, a director may be prosecuted for fraud or cooperative tax evasion; penalties include imprisonment and disqualification from managing companies in Spain for up to 10 years, non-cumulative with loss of public benefits.
AML / Modelo 232 Reporting and Public Contract Violation

Statutory sanction: Non-filing of Modelo 232: penalty from 1% to 5% of the total amount of related-party transactions, with minimums of €1,000 per data omission or inaccurate data, subject to a maximum of €100,000. AML omissions: administrative sanctions from €60,001 to €5,000,000 depending on entity size and seriousness, plus public debarment from contracting with public health authorities for up to 10 years. Bid-rigging (art. 262 Código Penal) imposes imprisonment from 6 months to 2 years, fines of up to 18 months' value, and special disqualification from public contracting for up to 10 years.

Director personal liability: Directors may be held personally liable for sanctions if they failed to prevent the AML deficiency; the financial penalty can be personally extended to directors who benefited from or tolerated the operation. For bid-rigging, the criminal sentence imposes automatic personal travel bans, prohibition on approaching the hospital contracting authority, and seizure of business assets; directors of the SL can be jointly ordered to compensate the public health authority up to the total project value. Travel bans and imprisonment remain applicable under the Spanish criminal procedural regime.
Failure to File / Late Filing of Modelo 200 and IRNR Formalities

Statutory sanction: Late filing surcharge: 10% within 3 months, plus 1% per additional month if no formal AEAT notice; 50% penalty if filed after AEAT request; 100% if filed after final assessment. Failure to withhold on dividend distributions to non-residents triggers a sanction equal to the unwithheld amount (up to 100% of the tax due), interest for late payment, and an infraction penalty of 50% of the amount. Personal liability may be shifted to the declarant administrator who signs the return with false data.

Director personal liability: Directors who instructed or participated in the omission of withholding on dividends or who signed fraudulent periodic returns are jointly and severally liable for the sanctions. In an aggravated criminal case, the director may face imprisonment of 1 to 4 years, a travel ban in Spanish territory, and mandatory judicial appearance; the court will additionally order the restoration of withheld sums to the Tax Agency, payable personally by the director if the company is insolvent.
